To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a Ca2+-inducible phosphoethanolaminetransferase (EptB) is required for the addition of a pEtN group to the outer Kdo residue of LPS in heptose-defective mutants and that this pEtN modification confers resistance to high Ca2+ concentrations.
the addition of a pEtN group to the outer Kdo residue of E. coli LPS is catalyzed by the periplasmically exposed EptB protein, which is homologous (but not orthologous) to the PmrC (EptA) protein.
a phosphoethano-lamine transferase (pEtN transferase), encoded by yhjW, adds a pEtN group to the outer Kdo residue of the lipopolysac- charide of an Escherichia coil mutant lacking heptose.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biosynthetic pathways that modify the lipid A moiety and the Kdo residues of LPS.
the identification of the genes encoding the enzymes responsible for the Ca2+-inducible modification of the outermost Kdo residue of LPS in heptose-defective E. coli.
the identification of a novel enzyme that adds a pEtN group to the outer Kdo of LPS in E. coli and the demonstration of its role in the protection of cells from high concentrations of CaCl2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pEtN modification is required for the protection of the cell against CaCl2 toxicity.
EptB is responsible for the pEtN modification at the outer Kdo residue in E. coli LPS.
EptB is the pEtN-transferase for the outer Kdo in the Ca2+ dependent pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
E. coli W3110 and WBB06 have two distinct pEtN transferases, EptA and EptB, which are responsible for pEtN modification in the core and outer Kdo domains, respectively.
pEtN transfer to the Kdo residue is an intrinsic property of E. coli LPS and is not dependent on the presence or absence of the heptose core.
E. coli EptB is a Ca2+-inducible phosphoethanolaminetransferase that modifies the Kdo residue of LPS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the outer Kdo of LPS is a site for the addition of a second pEtN unit, and this modification is important to the viability of cells with a heptoseless LPS core.
the pEtN modification at the Kdo2 residue of LPS in E. coli is not a random modification.
the pEtN residue of the Kdo2 residue of LPS is a critical factor that protects E. coli from the toxic effect of Ca2+.
